claims.text: Equal-atomic NbMoTaW is a single-phase BCC refractory high-entropy alloy.
NbMoTaW has excellent mechanical properties at high temperatures, including 1600 °C.
Equal-atomic NbMoTaW has poor room-temperature ductility.
The proposed intervention is to substitute approximately 5 at% Ti for one unspecified refractory element in NbMoTaW.
The modified alloy is to be produced by arc melting followed by homogenization.
Approximately 5 at% Ti will improve the room-temperature ductility of NbMoTaW.
Ti addition will activate additional dislocation slip systems at room temperature.
Ti addition will produce slight lattice distortion in the BCC NbMoTaW lattice.
The Ti-induced lattice modification will reduce the Peierls barrier for dislocation motion.
Lowering the dislocation activation barrier will enhance room-temperature dislocation mobility and ductility.
The Ti-modified alloy will preserve its overall BCC structure and phase stability at high temperature.
The Ti-modified alloy will retain mechanical performance comparable to untreated NbMoTaW at 1600 °C.
The lattice distortions considered important for irradiation resistance will be maintained after Ti addition.
The Ti-modified alloy will retain irradiation resistance comparable to untreated NbMoTaW.
The beneficial effect is restricted to controlled Ti levels near 5 at% and processing conditions that maintain phase stability.
Excessive Ti or nonuniform processing may destabilize the BCC phase or degrade high-temperature and irradiation behavior.
The magnitude of ductility improvement and changes in high-temperature yield strength will depend on Ti-distribution uniformity and processing conditions.
